chapter_theme: The three voids and tvam tat asi: the soul, the Supreme and their union, the three words of the saying, appear in turiya and are matched with maya, the beyond and peace, and with the letters of Om; when the impurities and qualities die Siva appears as darkness leaves before the moon, and the soul is known as Parasiva.
structure_note: 2488 sets out the three padas; 2489 and 2494 tie them to the impurities and the letters of Om; 2490 and 2491 give a practice of recitation and its fruit; 2492 and 2493 place the padas and give the Devadatta example.

2488.reading: Tat-pada, tvam-pada and asi-pada, which is itself: these three ancient padas appear in turiya; what stands in them is the soul, the Supreme and Siva who comes forth, and in these three threes the word-padas become tvam tat asi.
2488.nuance: The verse names the three words of the saying and matches them with soul, Supreme and Siva. Which pada goes with which is the tradition's reading of a compressed line.

2489.reading: In the three of tvam tat asi lie the old impurities beginning with kamya and the old qualities, and when these impurities and qualities die and Siva appears, it is like darkness going before the moon.
2489.nuance: காமியம் is the impurity of desire-born deeds. காமதம் in line 2 is doubtful; 2494 has தாமதம், and line 2 may name the qualities beginning with tamas. இந்து is the moon.

2490.reading: Bring forth tvam tat asi in the breath, reckon its order as tenfold, and recite the saying with its endless states before Siva in the order that moves it.
2490.nuance: வாசி may be the breath, as in the yoga of that name, or the utterance. ஈர்ஐந்து, ten, recalls the ten states of 2469. The practice described cannot be fixed from the verse.

2491.reading: Setting Siva within the bliss of one's own nature, and letting the teaching that is Om sink into a true heart, he knew the truth and stood, having become the Father's servant.
2491.nuance: மதி may be 'the mind' or 'the moon'. The verse ends in servitude (அடிமை), not in identity, which is worth noticing in a chapter on the soul becoming Parasiva.

2492.reading: Tvam-pada appears within maya, tat-pada rises in the beyond, asi-pada is reached in trusted peace: this is the saying tvam tat asi, spoken by the heavenly ones.
2492.nuance: அம்புரை is obscure; it is read here as the beyond. உம்பர் உரை may be the word of the gods or the word from above.

2493.reading: As in 'this is that Devadatta' the qualities that came between are let go, so when the body and its material cause are set aside, the true knowledge called tvam tat asi is that the soul is Parasiva.
2493.nuance: அச்சோயம் தேவதத்தன் is so'yam devadattah, 'this is that Devadatta', the standard example by which the saying's identity is explained: the same man seen in another time and place. Tirumular uses the Vedanta example within a Saiva frame.

2494.reading: The three great impurities, tamas, kamya and the dark quality, go with A, U and the vanishing M through the three bodies, and the turiya in which they are themselves is tvam tat asi.
2494.nuance: ஆசித்த குணம் is unclear. அகார, உகார, மகாரம் are the letters of Om; ஆம் அறும் மவ்வும், 'M that ends', and உடல் மூன்று, the three bodies, follow the mantra analysis. The line-by-line pairing is the tradition's.

links.note: Both argue identity through one man seen differently: 2485 one man in three roles, 2493 Devadatta recognised as the same man once changed circumstances are set aside.
Both name a set of three whose ending ends the trouble: the Kural desire, anger and delusion, whose very names must perish; Tirumular the impurities and qualities, whose dying lets Siva appear.

2489 says that when the malas and gunas die and Siva appears, it is like darkness going before the moon (இந்துவின் முன் இருள் ஏகுதல்). 1996 grants that moon, fire and sun remove black darkness but says Nandi removes the darkness that deeds make (செய்யிருள்). 2489 uses the moon as a likeness for Siva's coming, while 1996 sets Nandi above the moon, for a darkness it cannot reach.

2490 tells the seeker to bring forth தொந்தத்தசி in the breath (வாசியில் தோற்றி) and recite it before Siva. 2442 says that even some who do not know the fifty letters, seeking within the three-pada saying and driving the breath (வாசி செலுத்திட), become He by that supreme yoga. Both join the great saying to the breath; 2442 adds that this needs no learning of the letters.

2491 ends the one who took Om as teaching in servitude: he knew the truth and stood as the Father's servant (அத்தற்கு அடிமை அடைந்து நின்றானே). 2493, two verses on, ends the same practice of the saying in identity: the soul is Parasiva (சீவன் பரசிவன் ஆமே). The conflict holds if 2493 is read as strict identity; Siddhanta's union-without-identity can hold both.

2492 places tvam in maya, tat in the beyond, and asi-pada in trusted peace (அசிபதம் நம்புறு சாந்தியில் நண்ணும்). 2569 says it is tat-pada that is reached in the stilled state (தற்பதம் எய்து உபசாந்தத்து). The two assign the state of peace to different words of the saying; the conflict depends on taking சாந்தி and உபசாந்தம் as the same state.

2494 lists the great malas as தாமதம், காமியம் and a dark quality and places them with A, U and M in the turiya that is தொந்தத்தசி. 2489 says the impurities beginning with காமியம் and the qualities (தொல்கா மதமாதி, likely தாமதம்) lie in the three of தொந்தத்தசி, and Siva appears when they die. The same pair, kamya and tamas, is set inside the saying in both; 2494 adds the letters of Om, 2489 what happens when they die.

source_issues: Chapter title முச்சூனிய தொந்தத்தசி: the verses use தொந்தத்தசி (tvam tat asi) throughout.
2489 line 2: காமதம் may be an error for தாமதம், as in 2494.
2492: அம்புரை is obscure and may be corrupt.
